08/17/26|08/19/26||EDT|2|F|Y|Grand Rapids|MI|42.8775|-85.7627|OZONE||Good|No|FORECAST DISCUSSION:  The middle of August is upon us as schools start to open back up for students and summer slowly starts to transition into Fall. Before the change in seasons, however, summer temperatures will remain in place for the better half of this week. Low-80s to upper-70s will be felt across the state as a few rain chances make an appearance as well. On the backside of this front is another High-pressure which will hang around for the remainder of the work week. For air quality, Ozone does not look like it will pose a threat with cooler temperatures sprinkled in throughout this week. Also, the rain chances and shift in winds from the aforementioned front moving through on Wednesday will help clean out the atmosphere from any pollutant build up. PM2.5 looks like it will behave as well with Good to low-Moderate concentrations expected. Upper-level wildfire smoke may persist in the skies above this week, but it does look to be thinning out compared to recent weeks.   EXTENDED FORECAST: Another front moves through on Saturday bringing rain with it, but again, a washout is not expected. 08/17/26|08/19/26||EDT|2|F|Y|Ludington|MI|43.7646|-85.9954|OZONE||Good|No|FORECAST DISCUSSION:  The middle of August is upon us as schools start to open back up for students and summer slowly starts to transition into Fall. Before the change in seasons, however, summer temperatures will remain in place for the better half of this week. Low-80s to upper-70s will be felt across the state as a few rain chances make an appearance as well. Today, Monday, and tomorrow will have high-pressure dominating the weather regime as clear skies are expected for both days. Come midweek, a frontal boundary and low-pressure system will cross over the state on Wednesday providing rain showers, but not a complete washout. On the backside of this front is another High-pressure which will hang around for the remainder of the work week. For air quality, Ozone does not look like it will pose a threat with cooler temperatures sprinkled in throughout this week. Also, the rain chances and shift in winds from the aforementioned front moving through on Wednesday will help clean out the atmosphere from any pollutant build up. PM2.5 looks like it will behave as well with Good to low-Moderate concentrations expected. Upper-level wildfire smoke may persist in the skies above this week, but it does look to be thinning out compared to recent weeks.   EXTENDED FORECAST: Another front moves through on Saturday bringing rain with it, but again, a washout is not expected. Air quality will remain in the Good to Moderate range.|Michigan Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy

Clouds dominate Thursday, with surface air likely modified by overnight rain in the region, resulting in low ozone precursor concentrations and a capped ozone potential Thursday. 08/18/26|08/19/26||EDT|1|F|Y|Western Maryland|MD|39.6246|-78.9097|OZONE|42|Good|No|Sufficient sun and heat Wednesday will continue to build ozone pollution from local sources, though ozone into the Moderate range will be very isolated in nature due to an absence of any regional-scale ozone pollution, with most Maryland areas staying in the Good AQI range in the clean airmass.  A few hourly concentrations near the Bay and over northeast Maryland may push towards the upper Moderate, but daily average exposure will fall well short of the alert thresholds resulting in a Moderate AQI ozone forecast for the I-95 corridor, with Good AQI continuing elsewhere.  Clouds dominate Thursday, with surface air likely modified by overnight rain in the region, resulting in low ozone precursor concentrations and a capped ozone potential Thursday.  The result will be ozone concentrations soundly in the Good AQI range.  Some dry time on Friday may allow temperatures to get close to normal for the time of year, but still modest for ozone production.  With insufficient sun and increasing maritime air influence through the day, ozone will remain well within the Good AQI range.  Into Saturday a coastal system will keep the Good air quality trend.  Fine particle pollution and wildfire smoke concentrations across the country remain significantly diminished compared to recent weeks with no impacts from diffuse smoke expected in Maryland over the three-day forecast period. We coordinate to collectively share information for Washington communities affected by wildfire smoke. </description><link>https://wasmoke.blogspot.com/</link><managingEditor>noreply@blogger.com (Anonymous)</managingEditor><generator>Blogger</generator><openSearch:totalResults>827</openSearch:totalResults><openSearch:startIndex>1</openSearch:startIndex><openSearch:itemsPerPage>25</openSearch:itemsPerPage><item><guid isPermaLink="false">tag:blogger.com,1999:blog-7325117526675950090.post-4360899668909093957</guid><pubDate>Mon, 17 Aug 2026 18:30:45 +0000</pubDate><atom:updated>2026-08-17T11:30:45.213-07:00</atom:updated><title>Smoke continues in Central WA amid active fire conditions</title><description><p>Current smoke impacts are largely confined to areas downwind of active fires. The Little Giant and Sinlahekin Fires are the primary sources of smoke, and both are expected to produce more smoke today with warmer temperatures and increased winds.</p><table align="center" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" class="tr-caption-container" style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;"><tbody><tr><td style="text-align: center;"><a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/a/AVvXsEjovCbeg173CktZaIgsZ0Y5J3R95KCMqW4G_H_uwjixEYXQ6N2mJzo3ZiZAu8dZxq855VGqANgJcT4kvyNJT9HbclNzW1QQQDxbHs2M1BcdfU5XHicU6W8X7IrG5aEw9oxaeNMbMkeYQMVZUwvfQyVdBmJyuMMPoRzZ5fR-PZo7LB_spHZm-Yj4dhZZ-HfV" style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;"><img alt="" data-original-height="606" data-original-width="806" height="481" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/a/AVvXsEjovCbeg173CktZaIgsZ0Y5J3R95KCMqW4G_H_uwjixEYXQ6N2mJzo3ZiZAu8dZxq855VGqANgJcT4kvyNJT9HbclNzW1QQQDxbHs2M1BcdfU5XHicU6W8X7IrG5aEw9oxaeNMbMkeYQMVZUwvfQyVdBmJyuMMPoRzZ5fR-PZo7LB_spHZm-Yj4dhZZ-HfV=w640-h481" width="640" /></a></td></tr><tr><td class="tr-caption" style="text-align: center;">Large fires in the region. Source: DNR Wildfire Dashboard.</td></tr></tbody></table><br /><p></p><p><b><span style="font-size: medium;"><u>Fire Roundup</u></span></b></p><p>In the North Cascades, the <a href="https://inciweb.wildfire.gov/incident-information/wancp-border-2-fire" target="_blank">Border 2 Fire</a>, <a href="https://inciweb.wildfire.gov/incident-information/wancp-luna-fire" target="_blank">Luna Fire</a>, and <a href="https://inciweb.wildfire.gov/incident-information/waowf-ptarmigan-fire" target="_blank">Ptarmigan Fire</a> remain active, although recent rainfall has reduced fire activity.&nbsp;</p><p>The <a href="https://inciweb.wildfire.gov/incident-information/wanes-sinlahekin-fire" target="_blank">Sinlahekin Fire</a> west of Tonasket has grown to over 150,000 acres and is expected to remain active with warmer and drier conditions.</p><p>The <a href="https://inciweb.wildfire.gov/incident-information/waowf-little-giant-fire" target="_blank">Little Giant Fire</a> northwest of Leavenworth continues to expand and is now burning over130,000 acres. In addition to natural fire activity, burnout operations associated with efforts to protect structures and increase containment are contributing to additional smoke production.</p><p>Smoke production from the <a href="https://inciweb.wildfire.gov/incident-information/waowf-three-queens" target="_blank">Three Queens Fire</a> northwest of Little Kachess Lake (~3,600 acres) has decreased due to recent rain and firefighter efforts.</p><p>The <a href="https://inciweb.wildfire.gov/incident-information/wamrp-grand-park-2-fire" target="_blank">Grand Park 2 Fire</a> northeast of Mt. Rainier is now 57% contained and exhibiting moderate fire activity.</p><p>Further south, the <a href="https://inciweb.wildfire.gov/incident-information/wagpf-high-lava-fire" target="_blank">High Lava Fire</a> in Skamania County has grown to over 1,200 acres, but progress towards containment is increasing with cooler temperatures and increased moisture.</p><p>In Northeast WA, smoke production from the <a href="https://inciweb.wildfire.gov/incident-information/wanes-bradeen-hill-fire" target="_blank">Bradeen Hill</a>, <a href="https://inciweb.wildfire.gov/incident-information/wanes-hudspeth-fire" target="_blank">Hudspeth</a>, and <a href="https://inciweb.wildfire.gov/incident-information/waspa-mitre-rock-fire" target="_blank">Mitre Rock</a> Fires are minimal. The <a href="https://inciweb.wildfire.gov/incident-information/wacoa-modrite-fire" target="_blank">Modrite Fire</a> is currently 90% contained, and the <a href="https://inciweb.wildfire.gov/incident-information/wacoa-kaiser-canyon" target="_blank">Kaiser Canyon Fire</a> is also now 84% contained.&nbsp;</p><p>The <a href="https://inciweb.wildfire.gov/incident-information/orumf-paradise-fire" target="_blank">Paradise </a>and <a href="https://inciweb.wildfire.gov/incident-information/orumf-hagen-fire" target="_blank">Hagen</a> Fires in Northeast Oregon remain active; smoke from these fires may impact southeast WA later in the week.</p><p><b><span style="font-size: medium;"><u>Smoke Impacts</u></span></b></p><p>In <b>Central Washington</b>, smoke will persist in communities downwind of active fires. This includes Wenatchee, Leavenworth, Chelan, west Grant County, and across the Okanogan and Methow Valleys. Higher-elevation terrain along the Cascades will also remain smoky. While air quality may slightly improve in the afternoons, smoke will settle back into valleys overnight and into the early morning hours. <a href="https://forecast.weather.gov/wwamap/wwatxtget.php?cwa=OTX&amp;wwa=air%20quality%20alert" target="_blank">Air Quality Alerts</a> continue for Chelan, Douglas, Grant, and Okanogan Counties.&nbsp;</p><p>In <b>Northeast and Southeast Washington</b>, regional smoke transport may lead to hazy skies and moderate air quality, but no significant smoke intrusions are expected today or tomorrow.</p><p><b><span style="font-size: medium;"><u>Looking ahead</u></span></b></p><p>A warming and drying trend later this week will likely increase smoke production from active and emerging fires. Any new fires from lightning holdovers could grow quickly. We'll monitor air quality and update as the week progresses.</p><p></p><table align="center" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" class="tr-caption-container" style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;"><tbody><tr><td style="text-align: center;"><a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/a/AVvXsEiPXmBZF8TZ4O6yBW2wpkzHadWXzU0Pn8S0bkQmrSJoXK7Ndx8dachx-FcS57mreaxTeHYSS3PPT_t4UiWWlf0OjiIVlFRrCXX4YCEgOiV3ZV6lRQV53Lulj5df3oQ-kAdUmrI5wcELeJxKRN9o4CR3yIdHXoJg2QVFQF9cwnRjoiXeNqLwE4PRdM4dRLSV" style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;"><img alt="" data-original-height="1439" data-original-width="2209" height="416" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/a/AVvXsEiPXmBZF8TZ4O6yBW2wpkzHadWXzU0Pn8S0bkQmrSJoXK7Ndx8dachx-FcS57mreaxTeHYSS3PPT_t4UiWWlf0OjiIVlFRrCXX4YCEgOiV3ZV6lRQV53Lulj5df3oQ-kAdUmrI5wcELeJxKRN9o4CR3yIdHXoJg2QVFQF9cwnRjoiXeNqLwE4PRdM4dRLSV=w640-h416" width="640" /></a></td></tr><tr><td class="tr-caption" style="text-align: center;">Mountain embers on the Sinlahekin Fire. Source: Inciweb.</td></tr></tbody></table><br /><p></p></description><link>https://wasmoke.blogspot.com/2026/08/smoke-continues-in-central-wa-amid.html</link><author>noreply@blogger.com (Beth Friedman (Atmospheric Scientist - WA Ecology))</author><media:thumbnail xmlns:media="http://search.yahoo.com/mrss/" url="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/a/AVvXsEjovCbeg173CktZaIgsZ0Y5J3R95KCMqW4G_H_uwjixEYXQ6N2mJzo3ZiZAu8dZxq855VGqANgJcT4kvyNJT9HbclNzW1QQQDxbHs2M1BcdfU5XHicU6W8X7IrG5aEw9oxaeNMbMkeYQMVZUwvfQyVdBmJyuMMPoRzZ5fR-PZo7LB_spHZm-Yj4dhZZ-HfV=s72-w640-h481-c" height="72" width="72"/><thr:total>2</thr:total></item><item><guid isPermaLink="false">tag:blogger.com,1999:blog-7325117526675950090.post-3402540826406324424</guid><pubDate>Thu, 13 Aug 2026 17:45:29 +0000</pubDate><atom:updated>2026-08-13T15:51:14.528-07:00</atom:updated><title>Relief for NE WA, increased impacts across Central WA, and elevated smoke in Western WA</title><description><p>Eastern Washington is getting a bit of a reprieve from smoke today, but that improvement comes at the expense of areas along the Cascades. North and northeast winds are pushing smoke south and southwest, leading to smoky conditions this morning in places like Ellensburg, the Tri-Cities, and Yakima.</p><p>Yesterday's thunderstorms also resulted in lightning strikes mostly in North Central and Northeast WA. While no new fires have been reported as a result of the lightning, a Red Flag Warning through today for the Cascades and the Olympics could result in additional lightning strikes and new fire starts.</p><p></p><div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"><a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/a/AVvXsEjUTKceA5FT97kEsbn79AUvQmIDWfc-EAIV1e7co_EHNZeawr3f9GsQFUin6FG5ZkhMyVAx_8sxRkqMdF544FDMGIKu_YKWR0dASrG91Kyz90aEeSocxe7C-rT2bLGTw-AJrjnRKZpvpWiMtaJkaZhoPvjobev-NpTrsDmt8HV6n9Cs3-jM6qvGDaODqcSK" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"><img alt="" data-original-height="768" data-original-width="1024" height="480" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/a/AVvXsEjUTKceA5FT97kEsbn79AUvQmIDWfc-EAIV1e7co_EHNZeawr3f9GsQFUin6FG5ZkhMyVAx_8sxRkqMdF544FDMGIKu_YKWR0dASrG91Kyz90aEeSocxe7C-rT2bLGTw-AJrjnRKZpvpWiMtaJkaZhoPvjobev-NpTrsDmt8HV6n9Cs3-jM6qvGDaODqcSK=w640-h480" width="640" /></a></div><br /><p></p><p><b><span style="font-size: medium;">Smoke Outlook: Eastern WA</span></b></p><p>Smoke will continue drifting southwest throughout the day today and tomorrow. The greatest smoke impacts will continue to be in communities directly down wind of active fires, especially overnight and into the morning hours. However, communities to the north and northeast of active fires will see a period of improved air quality before southwest winds return this weekend.</p><p><a href="https://forecast.weather.gov/wwamap/wwatxtget.php?cwa=OTX&amp;wwa=air%20quality%20alert" target="_blank">Air Quality Alerts</a> continue for the majority of Central and Eastern WA, but these may be revised as the day progresses. While occasional clearing and intermittent good air quality is possible during periods of stronger winds, smoke production continues to be significant from regional fires. Be sure to check air quality monitors before outdoor activities.</p><p><i>UPDATE 3:30 pm: Air Quality Alerts are no longer in effect for Adams, Klickitat, Lincoln, Pend Oreille, Spokane, and Whitman Counties.</i></p><p><b><span style="font-size: medium;">Smoke Outlook: Western WA</span></b></p><p>Smoke is filtering into western WA. Currently, the majority of the smoke is aloft in the atmosphere, producing hazy skies and vibrant sunrises and sunsets. Puget Sound Clean Air Agency's ceilometer at Marysville shows the smoke layer about 1500 m above the surface.</p><table align="center" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" class="tr-caption-container" style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;"><tbody><tr><td style="text-align: center;"><a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhnhPcBHTv_m4YP3hPOPWXv8CyFLV-x-9UEffh1w74oeIKWcBFZlrm8R0nCvXxcNBtoMwMA4qjewylTM1f_M6cuK7GVl0gAnC9GRNiOEXiSsLJg02UJTrTvD4Q0tGedEc4Y3REuhtYyRQoGnmkOh1QddGrucNW3CeK3yI5NQ7nniKkFHGePrklf2lsC7jnq/s3248/ceilometer.png" style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;"><img border="0" data-original-height="1857" data-original-width="3248" height="366" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhnhPcBHTv_m4YP3hPOPWXv8CyFLV-x-9UEffh1w74oeIKWcBFZlrm8R0nCvXxcNBtoMwMA4qjewylTM1f_M6cuK7GVl0gAnC9GRNiOEXiSsLJg02UJTrTvD4Q0tGedEc4Y3REuhtYyRQoGnmkOh1QddGrucNW3CeK3yI5NQ7nniKkFHGePrklf2lsC7jnq/w640-h366/ceilometer.png" width="640" /></a></td></tr><tr><td class="tr-caption" style="text-align: center;"><i><span>Ceilometer data from Marysville. Courtesy PSCAA.</span></i></td></tr></tbody></table><br /><p>The most noticeable smoke impacts will occur in the foothills, Cascades, the eastern portions of Skagit and Whatcom counties, and higher elevations. Smoke will also be present in the Olympics until tomorrow afternoon.&nbsp;While some daytime mixing may bring smoke down to the surface in the Puget Sound and push conditions into Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups for several hours, widespread poor air quality is not expected. Today's pattern will continue into tomorrow as smoke drifting southwest mixes with a weak push of cleaner marine air. Onshore winds return Saturday morning to clear out any lingering haze or moderate surface impacts.&nbsp;</p><p><a href="https://nwcleanairwa.gov/" target="_blank">Northwest Clean Air Agency&nbsp;</a>has issued an Air Quality Alert for Skagit and Whatcom Counties through Saturday at 9am. <a href="https://www.swcleanair.gov/docs/NewsReleases/2026-08-13%20Air%20Quality%20Advisory%20for%20Wildfire%20Smoke%20News%20Release.pdf" target="_blank">Southwest Clean Air Agency</a> has also issued an air quality alert for wildfire smoke for Skamania County through tomorrow evening with intermittent impacts also expected in the eastern portions of Clark, Cowlitz, and Lewis counties.&nbsp;</p><table align="center" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" class="tr-caption-container" style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;"><tbody><tr><td style="text-align: center;"><a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjLxrT6eunEleK3hyS_RvrlWjXE6WpJI-svz5SRr2eLzc4FSDBkZFWT7boeP8J-StwiQHt0ZCKBXVhDg1gNDzdjZBn9Fy2PZUJQBDwiAw81l3Y-ZgtSvOe__uSW-BNbheVQuNLaEGrmTF6nbxOODr_Y9qczqih2OPogr2fZXM2ot_gmFEixtk6n-1V3sySs/s1857/xsection.png" style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;"><img border="0" data-original-height="1857" data-original-width="1856" height="640" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjLxrT6eunEleK3hyS_RvrlWjXE6WpJI-svz5SRr2eLzc4FSDBkZFWT7boeP8J-StwiQHt0ZCKBXVhDg1gNDzdjZBn9Fy2PZUJQBDwiAw81l3Y-ZgtSvOe__uSW-BNbheVQuNLaEGrmTF6nbxOODr_Y9qczqih2OPogr2fZXM2ot_gmFEixtk6n-1V3sySs/w640-h640/xsection.png" width="640" /></a></td></tr><tr><td class="tr-caption" style="text-align: center;"><span><i>Cross-section from the HRRR smoke model, valid at 3pm Friday afternoon. Smoke impacts will mostly be aloft in the atmosphere with the greatest impacts at higher elevations. A weather system will bring scattered thunderstorms across Northern Washington and BC this week, but the amount of precipitation will likely not be enough to abate fire activity.&nbsp; Lightning could also spark new fires near the Canadian border.&nbsp;<br /><br /></p><div class="separator" style="clear: both; Minimize the health risks to workers by reducing exposure time to wildfire smoke. Each workplace is unique and requires a unique approach in protecting their workers from wildfire smoke. The following are some suggestions:</div><p></p><p style="font-size: 12pt; margin-bottom: 0px; margin-top: 0px; text-align: left;"></p><p></p><p></p><ul style="text-align: left;"><li><span style="font-family: inherit;">Provide enclosed buildings, structures, or vehicles with filtered air;</span></li></ul><ul style="text-align: left;"><li><span style="font-family: inherit;">Relocate work to less smoky areas;</span></li></ul><ul style="text-align: left;"><li><span style="font-family: inherit;">Reschedule work for a time with less smoke pollution;</span></li></ul><ul style="text-align: left;"><li><span style="font-family: inherit;">Avoid work that creates dust, fumes, or smoke;&nbsp;</span></li></ul><ul style="text-align: left;"><li><span style="font-family: inherit;">Reduce work intensity;</span></li></ul><ul style="text-align: left;"><li><span style="font-family: inherit;">Provide additional rest periods; and</span></li></ul><ul style="text-align: left;"><li><span style="font-family: inherit;">Provide respirators, such as an N95.</span></li></ul><p></p><p></p><p style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: inherit;">The Department of Labor &amp; Industries' rules for wildfire smoke are based on a datapoint called PM2.5, which is a measure of particle matter present in the air that is 2.5 microns or smaller.
